record.paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
record.original_question: Let N be a closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link, and assume that the complement of the singular locus is atoroidal. Under this extra topological hypothesis, is the anti-de Sitter geometry of N rigid relative to the tachyon masses?

evidence.quote: Question 9.3. Let N be a closed AdS manifold with tachyons, so that the singular locus is a link. Further, assume that the complement of the singular locus is atoroidal. Is the AdS geometry of N rigid relative to the tachyon mass?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. An anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure on a 3-manifold is a Lorentzian metric of constant sectional curvature −1; equivalently, a (G,X)-structure modeled on AdS_3 = PSL(2,R) with isometry group PSL(2,R) × PSL(2,R). A closed AdS 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link L ⊂ N is a closed 3-manifold N together with an AdS structure on N ∖ L whose holonomy around each component γ_i of L is a Lorentzian "boost-type" rotation; the conjugacy class of this holonomy is parametrized by a positive real number m_i > 0, the tachyon mass of γ_i. (Locally near γ_i, the metric has a model singularity of constant curvature −1 with a cone-like Lorentzian singular axis of mass m_i.)

The AdS structure is said to be rigid relative to the tachyon masses if any two such closed AdS structures on N with tachyon link L and the same prescribed tachyon masses (m_1, …, m_k) are isometric (equivalently, equivalent as marked AdS structures up to isotopy).

A 3-manifold M with toral boundary is atoroidal if every embedded incompressible torus in M is boundary-parallel.

Problem. Let N be a closed AdS 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link L ⊂ N, and assume that the complement N ∖ L is atoroidal. Is the AdS geometry of N rigid relative to the tachyon masses (m_1, …, m_k) of the components of L?
artifact.status_search_result: A current University of Vienna research project explicitly lists the study of rigidity/flexibility of closed AdS 3-manifolds with link-type tachyons as an active research direction, indicating the question has not yet been settled. No published proof of rigidity (or of a counterexample) under the atoroidal-complement hypothesis was found.

status_evidence.title: Rigidity and flexibility of anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds — University of Vienna
status_evidence.snippet: The research focuses on the study of the rigidity and flexibility of globally hyperbolic, compact AdS three-manifolds with smooth convex boundary and that of closed AdS three-manifolds with link-type tachyons.
status_evidence.claim: AdS rigidity with tachyon singularities is an ongoing research project, suggesting the question remains open.
